fix.notes: Stripping category 'S' also removes math symbols (Sm) like ± and currency symbols (Sc) like £. These are extremely rare in Magic deck names so the impact is negligible, but a reviewer should be aware. The fix is applied at rendering time only — stored deck names are not modified.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

Deck names (and potentially archetype/person names) containing emoji or Unicode symbol characters (e.g. `✋` in "Stop That✋") were passed through verbatim into the HTML `<title>` tag and OpenGraph `og:title`/`og:description` meta tags. This caused big yellow emoji to appear in Chrome browser tabs and Google search result snippets, which looks unprofessional.

## What changed

- Added `strip_unsafe_chars(s: str) -> str` in `decksite/view.py` — strips any character whose Unicode category starts with `'S'` (Symbol: Sm, Sc, Sk, So). This removes emoji and pictographs while preserving CJK, Greek, Cyrillic, and all letter/number characters.
- Applied it in `View.title()` so the browser `<title>` is always clean.
- Applied it in `Deck.og_title()`, `Deck.og_description()`, `Archetype.og_title()`, and `Archetype.og_description()` to cover OpenGraph metadata.
- Added unit tests covering the exact example from the issue (`Stop That✋`), plain ASCII, and preservation of CJK/Greek/Cyrillic.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed (all checks)
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit decksite/view_test.py` — 846 passed, 1 skipped
- New test `test_strip_unsafe_chars_removes_emoji` passes explicitly.

Fixes #12580
